composition.story: A parent node holds 10 samples, 5 A and 5 B. We compute its Gini impurity. Then a split sends 6 samples left and 4 right. We compute each side's Gini and weight it by size. Information gain is the parent Gini minus that weighted average: 0.500 − 0.417 = 0.083.

aha.observation: Information gain is the parent Gini minus the size-weighted child Gini: 0.500 − 0.417 = 0.083, so this split reduces impurity.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons. Names stay the same when disabled at the first or last step. Keyboard: Left and Right arrow keys.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Goes back to step 1, Parent node.

states.label: Parent node
states.sentence: The parent node holds 10 samples: 5 of class A and 5 of class B.
states.why: Impurity measures how mixed the classes are before the split.

states.label: Parent Gini
states.sentence: Gini is 1 minus the sum of squared class shares: 1 − (0.5² + 0.5²) = 0.500.
states.why: A 50/50 mix gives the highest Gini possible for two classes.

states.label: Apply split
states.sentence: The split sends 6 samples left (4 A, 2 B) and 4 samples right (1 A, 3 B).
states.why: Each child is scored on its own class counts.

states.label: Left Gini
states.why: Mostly A, so it is purer than the parent.

states.label: Right Gini
states.why: Mostly B, so it is also purer than the parent.

states.label: Weighted average
states.sentence: Weight each side by its share of samples: 0.6 × 0.444 + 0.4 × 0.375 = 0.417.
states.why: Bigger children affect the split's score more.

states.label: Information gain
states.sentence: Gain = parent Gini − weighted child Gini = 0.500 − 0.417 = 0.083.
states.why: A positive gain means the split lowers impurity. The tree picks the split with the largest gain.
